source.title: M3: A State-Event Generative Foundation Model for Market Microstructure Dynamics
source.authors: Yanzhi Zhang; Yu Ma; Yi-Lin Cheng; Jian Li; Yi-Tong Duan

record.tranche_reason: The study fits and evaluates scaling behavior in an autoregressive market microstructure model trained on order-event data, extending scaling-law tests beyond text language models.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a 5-size by 4-token-budget validation-loss grid, a fitted scaling law, and held-out-size prediction errors. The grid’s individual loss values appear only in Figure 3. Downstream results are not rows for V6 because they do not relate downstream performance to model scale or pretraining loss.
record.test_reason: The study trains autoregressive Transformers (9.66M–1.27B parameters) on tokenized financial order events, fits a Chinchilla-style L(N,D) law to a 5×4 validation-loss grid, and checks held-out-size prediction. This is a new, non-text setting with its own result on the power-law form (V5) and on extrapolation to a larger size (V2).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors say M3 shows predictable scaling and that a Chinchilla-style law in model size and training tokens characterizes validation loss. They add that held-out-size prediction errors are below about 1%.
record.recipe_differences: Fits a Chinchilla-style law to market-model validation loss over a 5-by-4 model-size/token grid; reports leave-one-model-size-out validation and residual bootstrap uncertainty. It is an extension to financial order-event modeling, not a reproduction of the original language-model experiments.
record.problems: Only one loss observation is available per configuration, so the reported bootstrap intervals do not capture run-to-run training stochasticity. Individual grid loss values are shown only in a figure.

untested.parts: Extrapolation across orders of magnitude. Only a 3.5× parameter extrapolation is tested, with no token-budget extrapolation.
Image/video, repeated-data, fine-tuning and transfer regimes. The form is tested only over about 2 orders of magnitude in N and 1.5 in D, single seed. Figure 4 multi-epoch curves are not fitted.
Not tested: the subject is not a text language model.
No compute-optimal N/D allocation is derived or evaluated.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Downstream diagnostics are reported only for one model, not related to scale or loss.
Only one fitting setup (Huber on log-loss residuals). Alternative fits are not compared and no curvature is tested.

missing.what: Leave-one-model-size-out MAPEs: 1.14%, 0.40%, 0.56%, 0.70%, 0.53% (mean 0.66%). The 9.66M fold is a lower-end extrapolation.
Training/validation loss and perplexity curves over four epochs (repeated data) for all five sizes. Figure only, not fitted.

record.verdict_notes: Single run per configuration; the bootstrap CIs exclude seed variance. Loss is next-token cross-entropy over a 32,768-code VQ vocabulary of order events, so the absolute values are not comparable to text LMs. No compute-optimal analysis is given even though the Chinchilla form is used. The reader's V2 limits_scope label was removed: the untested orders-of-magnitude range is listed as untested rather than as a scope limit.

versions.untested_parts: The study models financial order-event sequences, not held-out pretraining loss of language models.
The largest reported extrapolation is from models up to 366.06M parameters to 1.27B, not runs orders of magnitude larger.
The study fits loss against model size and token count but does not identify or evaluate the loss-minimizing parameter/token allocation at fixed compute.
No comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count is reported.
The study tests scaling only for its market microstructure order-event modeling setup; it does not test image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Downstream prediction diagnostics are reported, but their relationship to scale or pretraining loss is not tested.
The study reports one fitting setup and its uncertainty; it does not compare fitting choices or demonstrate curves bending away from a power law.

rows.subject: M3
rows.operation_detail: Fit a Chinchilla-style loss function to validation losses across model size and training-token budget.
rows.value: L(N, D) = 5.3697 + 1.0027/N^0.3795 + 1.5987/D^0.3117; N is parameters in millions and D is training tokens in billions.
rows.locator: Scaling Law, Equation (2); Evaluation Details—Scaling Law
rows.note: The complete observed grid comprises 20 losses; the paper says it fits a Chinchilla-style law to those validation losses.
rows.check: Fitted law with bootstrap CIs. The range is about 2 orders of magnitude in N (9.66M–1.27B) and about 1.5 in D (1B–31.9B), with one run per cell. Note that E=5.37 dominates the loss (losses about 5.8–7.2).

rows.subject: M3
rows.size_stated: Fit uses models up to 366.06M parameters; held-out model has 1.27B parameters
rows.operation_detail: Fit on smaller model sizes and predict validation losses for the held-out 1.27B model.
rows.value: MAPE 0.53%; maximum absolute relative error 1.12%. Signed errors at 1B, 3B, 10B, and 31.9B tokens: +1.12%, −0.11%, −0.27%, and +0.60%.
rows.note: This tests extrapolation from smaller to larger models, but the held-out model is about 3.5 times the largest model used for fitting, not orders of magnitude larger.
rows.check: Should also link V5, since it is predictive validation of the power-law form in this modality. The extrapolation is only about 3.5× in N (366M→1.27B).

source_check.correct: MAPE 0.53%; maximum absolute relative error 1.12%; signed errors +1.12%, −0.11%, −0.27%, +0.60% at 1B, 3B, 10B, 31.9B tokens. State observed is appropriate for V5. Remove the V2 link: extrapolation from 366.06M to 1.27B does not test prediction orders of magnitude beyond the fitting sizes.
source_check.problem: The measurements are correct, but observed overstates evidence for V2's explicitly required extrapolation over orders of magnitude.
